newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-LENNOX LEWIS TRAINER SAYS TYSON SANCTIONS FAIR.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-LENNOX LEWIS TRAINER SAYS TYSON SANCTIONS FAIR.

text.p: Emanuel Steward, manager or trainer of 27 world champions during three decades, took time out from his final preparations with his current charge, Briton Lennox Lewis, to weigh in on the Mike Tyson sanctions Wednesday.

"I felt that it was a most fair and accurate decision that he received," said Steward after the Nevada State Athletic Commission revoked Tyson's boxing license for at least one year and fined him $3 million for biting Evander Holyfield's ears in their World Boxing Association title bout.
"Two years or more would not have been fair," said Steward, who is training Lewis, the World Boxing Council heavyweight champion, for his bout against Henry Akinwande Saturday at Stateline, Nevada.
Steward believes Tyson can earn the right to fight again after one year, when state commmission regulations allow him to apply for relicensing.
"I feel if he stays clean, he'll be reinstated in one year," said Steward, who also trains former four-time world champion Thomas Hearns and current WBC welterweight champ Oscar De La Hoya.

"Anything other than one year would have ended his career, considering he spent three years of incarceration," said Steward, referring to the 31-year-old former world heavyweight champion's prison time for rape.

"I believe the punishment he received (from the state commission) was a very good choice considering he had never been in a suspension situation before. It was the first time he was involved in a boxing violation. He never had a history of fouling a guy."
Tyson has said the bites were in retaliation for head butts that opened a gash over his right eyelid but went unpunished in the June 28 bout, from which he was disqualified.
"Let me make this perfectly clear, that he was butted accidentally," said Steward.
"But Tyson was provoked and was in a retaliatory situation. He felt he was handicapped the final nine rounds and wanted Evander to be handicapped, too.
"He was upset and shocked when he got disqualified. He never expected it. He felt he would just get cautioned. When he was disqualified, he went beserk. That's what I read from Mike's actions."
